text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein says Jordan's relations with United Arab Emirates are as good and solid as possible; Middle East peace process is very important and all agreements should be implemented.
- Carpet donated by King Hussein leaves for Jerusalem's Al-Aqsa mosque.
- Row between electricians' union and company likely to be referred to labour arbitration.
- Town and planning law to be presented to the government soon contains amendments to land exclusion within municipality borders.
- King Hussein and UAE's Sheikh Zaid affirm the need to concentrate efforts to push forward the peace process.
- Iraqi Trade Minister Saleh says Aqaba to be considered a principle port for Iraqi imports alongside its Gulf port of Umm Qasr.
- Saleh says Jordanian goods will be bought by Iraq under U.N. oil-for-food deal but no guarantees given and no quotas allocated to Jordanian imports.
- Jordan, UAE want Iraq to take "legal, political" steps to reassure world public opinion, Prime Minister Kabariti says.
- Opposition decries Israeli participation in exhibition of weapons and equipment.
